newsitem.title: USA: MSRB eyeing NYS senator's report on pay-to-play.
newsitem.headline: MSRB eyeing NYS senator's report on pay-to-play.

text.p: The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's executive director said the 15-member panel, which is scheduled to meet for a quarterly meeting at the end of the month, is being briefed on a new report alleging "pay-to-play" in New York State.
"We supply the board with information on everything that's happened and reported," Christopher Taylor said in a telephone interview. "We will make them aware of this. They are already aware of it."

New York State Sen. Franz Leichter, D-Manhattan, issued a report on Wednesday that said state Republicans got almost $1 million in campaign contributions in 1995 and 1996 from municipal bond firms that were awarded profitable underwriting contracts.

Leichter said Republicans "got around" the board's rule G-37 by soliciting contributions to an " elaborate web of committees controlled by the State GOP. Rule G-37 bars firms from making contributions to state officials within two years of winning any negotiated bond business in that state.
Rule G-37 does not bar contributions to political parties. But under a recent amendment to the rule, dealers must report gifts to parties quarterly to the MSRB.
The board said that if a contribution is "earmarked or known to be provided to a particular issuer" then the dealer would be violating rule G-37.
The board said it wanted to amend the rule because of reports that pay-to-play problems are "emerging in connection with the fundraising practices of certain political parties."
